name: Shoreditch
description: Buzzing East London hub of startups, galleries, and bars. Fast-paced, expensive, and very well connected.

name: Wimbledon
description: Leafy suburb with a village feel, good schools, and easy rail links into central London.

name: Canary Wharf
description: Glass-tower financial and tech district with modern flats, riverside walks, and a growing residential scene.

name: Clapham
description: Popular with young professionals for its common, bars, and quick tube access to the centre.

name: Chiswick
description: Riverside, village-like West London suburb favoured by families, with strong schools and a low-key pace.

name: Walthamstow
description: Up-and-coming area with a large market, reservoirs and parks, and some of the better value rents inside the North East London zones.

name: Brixton
description: Vibrant, multicultural area known for its market, music scene, and relatively good value for zone 2.

name: Northern Quarter
description: Manchester's creative and indie scene — record shops, bars, and a growing tech and media crowd.

name: Didsbury
description: Popular South Manchester suburb with parks, good schools, and a village high street.

name: MediaCityUK / Salford Quays
description: Waterside media and tech campus (BBC, ITV) with modern apartments and a growing digital scene.

name: Digbeth
description: Birmingham's creative quarter — converted warehouses, street art, and a fast-growing tech and startup scene.

name: Edgbaston
description: Leafy area home to the university and cricket ground, popular with families and postgraduate students.

name: Leith
description: Historic port area turned foodie and creative hotspot, with waterside walks and a strong sense of community.

name: Morningside
description: Genteel Edinburgh suburb with independent shops, good schools, and easy access to the Meadows and hills.

name: Stokes Croft
description: Bristol's street-art and independent culture heartland, known for its murals, bars, and alternative scene.

name: Clifton
description: Georgian-terrace neighbourhood near the Suspension Bridge, popular with families and professionals.

name: Leeds City Centre
description: Compact, walkable centre with a fast-growing finance and tech sector and a lively bar and restaurant scene.

name: Headingley
description: Popular with students and young renters, with parks, cricket, and a busy independent food scene.

name: West End
description: Bohemian university district with parks, independent cafes, and some of Glasgow's best-value period flats.

name: Reading Town Centre
description: Thames Valley tech hub with a fast direct rail line into London, popular with commuters and tech workers.
